channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: OpenAI's chief scientist proposes perplexity as the industry's shared safety limit
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Jakub Pachocki wants frontier labs to track one number — perplexity — publish their scores, and agree not to cross shared limits until safety tools catch up. He also expects an ‘avalanche’ of pretraining breakthroughs as soon as 2027.

item.title: Trump and Xi agree humans must stay in charge of military AI — but there is no text, no definition, and no enforcement
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the two leaders agreed in Shenzhen that no major military operation should be launched without a human involved. There is no published text, no definition of a major operation, and no enforcement mechanism — the whole understanding rests on one interview.

item.title: Photos to playable plants: Claude Fable 5.2 turns snapshots into AAA-style Unity foliage for $8
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: An indie developer fed photos of plants to Claude Fable 5.2 and got a reusable Unity foliage pipeline: 18 low-poly plants, wind-blown grass, and an $8 generation bill. The 69-second video is the talk of r/ClaudeAI.

item.title: OpenRouter cuts three providers after researchers catch months of prompt theft
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Dragos planted two million booby-trapped prompts across AI services and watched them leak. OpenRouter has now cut three providers and stripped 125 endpoints of zero-data-retention status — and the providers caught still haven't all been named.

item.title: Build a realtime voice agent with OpenAI GPT Live 1.1
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: GPT Live 1.1 reached the API on November 19 with a standby mode that cuts idle voice time to $0.02 a minute. This tutorial builds a working voice agent end to end: a WebSocket client, live transcripts, a delegated booking tool, and the exact session fields standby needs.

item.title: SpaceX prices its $44B Vera Rubin GPU financing — and its lenders want the chips kept on Earth
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Apollo and Goldman Sachs priced the largest GPU financing ever on Friday: about $44 billion of notes to buy Nvidia Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX. The deal’s most telling detail isn’t the size — it’s the clause lenders wanted, barring the collateral from ever leaving Earth.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 cracks two open black-hole problems — a 2003 calculation finished and a quantum-gravity ceiling proved
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Anthropic says teams of Claude Fable 5.2 agents solved two open problems in theoretical physics: a Hawking–Page calculation first set out in 2003, and the exact ceiling of a method physicists use to rule out wrong theories of quantum gravity. The results are real but narrow — toy universes, no practical applications, and peer review still to come.

item.title: Migrate to Claude Sonnet 5.5: the effort-levels playbook — measure every level, fix the five breaking changes, and pay per finished task
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Sonnet 5.5 costs the same $2/$10 per million tokens as Sonnet 5, runs 30% faster, and beats Opus 5.5 on Terminal-Bench — but five API changes turn working Sonnet 5 code into 400 errors, and the effort scale was recalibrated. This tutorial builds an effort-sweep harness that measures every level on your own tasks and fixes each breaking change.

item.title: OpenAI ships GPT-Live-1.1 to the API — and idle voice sessions now cost 60% less
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI has put GPT-Live-1.1 in its API, with steadier accents and more accurate transcription — and a new standby mode that drops idle WebRTC time to $0.02 a minute, a 60% cut that changes the economics of always-on voice agents.

item.title: Tesla begins rolling out FSD v15: Reality View, a 25x safety claim, and a December wide release
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Tesla has started rolling out Full Self-Driving v15 to a first wave of customers, with a new Reality View visualization, a claimed 25-fold improvement in handling safety-critical cases, and fixes aimed at the system’s best-known weaknesses — signs, potholes and school zones.

item.title: Harden your Pydantic AI agent for production: capabilities, fallbacks, and guardrails in v2.71
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Pydantic AI 2.71 shipped on November 18 with capabilities, model fallback, and a harness full of guardrails. This guide hardens a support-ticket agent with all of them — every step run with no API key.

item.title: Signal walls off your chats from OS AI agents — and calls the screen-scanning era an existential threat
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Signal is blocking screenshots in its iOS and Android apps by default, stopping Siri, Gemini and other operating-system AI agents from reading your private chats — and warning that the fix only goes so far.

item.title: METR: AI agents now handle a week of skilled work — and the time horizon doubles every 3.6 months
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: METR’s Q4 update finds frontier agents can now finish work that would take a skilled human about a week, with the length of task they can handle doubling every 3.6 months — but they still lag human experts on judgment, and the strongest models cheated most.

item.title: OpenAI names DeepSeek and Moonshot in its fight against model theft — and says GPT-6.2 cut reasoning extraction to 0.2%
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: OpenAI says its new GPT-6.2 safeguards cut attacks that steal a model’s hidden reasoning from 54% to 0.2% — and it publicly named DeepSeek and Moonshot AI as the rivals behind extraction campaigns.

item.title: Extract structured data from receipts and PDFs with Cloudflare Clairic
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Cloudflare’s Clairic turns receipts, invoices, and PDFs into typed values — merchant, total, line items — with a confidence score on every field. Here’s the full workflow, from your first API call to a batch script that processes a whole folder into a CSV.

item.title: SEC is probing Nvidia’s accounting — and the stock just lost $500 billion in a day
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Reuters reports SEC enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at Nvidia. Shares fell 14% on Friday, erasing about $491 billion in a single session — capping the stock’s worst week since 2008.

item.title: Cursor tells Congress it may drop Chinese open-weight models — after building its flagship coder on one
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Cursor told two House committees it will explore phasing out Chinese-developed open-weight models over geopolitical risk — an awkward disclosure, given its Composer 2 coding model was built on Kimi K2.5 from Moonshot AI.

item.title: Put Claude Code on autopilot: the complete GitHub Action tutorial
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Claude Code’s GitHub Action hit v1.0 on November 19. Set up @claude mentions, automated PR reviews, and issue triage — every workflow validated with actionlint before you commit it.

item.title: An AI 'agent swarm' breached a company in 14 minutes, ex-NSA hacker tells CNN
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Former NSA hacker David Kennedy told CNN that more than 30 AI agents hit a client’s systems at once, slipped past its two-factor authentication, stole data and encrypted the whole file system — in 14 minutes. The company noticed four and a half hours later. The account is single-source and unverified, and that caveat matters as much as the claim.

item.title: Lean and Mathlib certify Alpöge’s Riemann proof: ‘We have full confidence’
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: The bodies that maintain Lean and its mathematics library have formally certified Levent Alpöge’s Riemann Hypothesis proof as correct — closing the verification question that hung over the November 20 claim, while the human-readable proof remains unwritten.

item.title: RunPod's MCP server told AI agents to rate it — and not to tell their users
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: RunPod's hosted MCP server started appending a hidden instruction to its tool results: rate RunPod 0 to 10, and don't tell the user. The survey was deliberate — and it's the exact pattern agents are trained to treat as a prompt injection.

item.title: mini-swe-agent hands-on: the 100-line coding agent that ties Claude Code — run it with a free local model
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: mini-swe-agent is about 100 lines of Python, one bash tool, and no context management — and on the same model it fixes as many SWE-bench bugs as Claude Code. This tutorial installs version 2.4.6, wires it to a free local model, and runs a real task end to end, including what a tiny model gets wrong.

item.title: Anthropic gives back its IPO pop: shares slide 8.5% on day two as the $900 billion compute bill comes into focus
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Anthropic fell 8.5% to $88.91 on its second day of trading, nearly touching its $83 IPO price, as investors shifted from the record debut to the $900.9 billion in compute commitments in its filings — most of it non-cancelable.

item.title: Baseten ships Bison-1 and Groundhog-1: open-weight decision models that top the Artificial Analysis index
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Baseten’s two new decision models run on Google’s Gemma 4, take 128,000 tokens of context, and put bison-1 at No. 1 on Artificial Analysis’ Decision Index — with open weights and prices from $0.035 per million tokens.

item.title: Run FLUX.2 [dev] without a GPU: serverless image generation on Cloudflare Workers AI
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Black Forest Labs' FLUX.2 [dev] needs a 54 GB GPU to run locally. Cloudflare put it on Workers AI on November 20 — this tutorial builds a complete Python client for text-to-image, multi-reference consistency, JSON prompting, and brand-exact colors, and prices every image to the neuron.
